headline: Writing is only 5,000 years old—it transformed human civilization almost overnight
universal_truth: The ability to preserve ideas beyond memory changes everything
fun_facts: Writing was invented independently at least three times—in Mesopotamia, China, and Mesoamerica
The first writing was for accounting, not literature—tracking grain and taxes
Most of human history happened before writing; we call that 'prehistory'
discussion_questions: How would your life be different without writing?
What ideas can only exist because of writing?
Is digital communication changing writing again?

hook.script: For 95% of human history, we had no writing. Every idea, every story, every piece of knowledge existed only in living memory. Then, about 5,000 years ago, humans made marks that could carry meaning across time. Everything changed.

cliff.script: Humans spoke for at least 100,000 years before inventing writing. What finally triggered this breakthrough? And why did it happen in multiple places around the same time?

options.text: Growing civilizations needed to track property, debts, and transactions beyond memory
options.response: Yes. The first writing was for accounting. Commerce and administration drove the invention.

options.text: People wanted to preserve their stories and religious beliefs
options.response: Literature came later. The earliest writing was for practical record-keeping...

fact1.title: Accounting Origins
fact1.script: The earliest writing—Sumerian cuneiform, about 3400 BCE—tracked grain, livestock, and debts. Poetry came centuries later. Writing was invented not for beauty but for business. Bureaucracy created literature.

fact2.title: Multiple Inventions
fact2.script: Writing was invented independently at least three times: Mesopotamia, China, and Mesoamerica. Each developed unique systems without contact. When civilizations reach certain complexity, writing seems to emerge.

fact3.title: Memory Externalized
fact3.script: Before writing, knowledge died with the knower. Writing externalizes memory—ideas survive their thinkers. Laws, discoveries, and stories persist across millennia. The books you read may contain minds thousands of years old.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Writing preserves ideas beyond the limits of memory and life. When you write, you're using humanity's most powerful memory technology. What you record might outlast you by centuries.

outro.script: That's Day 94. Tomorrow, we'll discover what reading does to your brain. Until then, appreciate that you can access minds from thousands of years ago through squiggles on surfaces.

growTrack.title: Writing Preservation - Record What Matters
growTrack.learning_objective: Use writing intentionally to preserve important ideas
growTrack.activity: What idea, experience, or insight would you want preserved beyond your memory? Write it down today. A journal entry, a note, a letter. Writing is how we speak to the future.
